title: What If a Giant Space Mirror Lit Up the Night? Russia Tried

scenes.text: What if a mirror in space could turn night into day? In 1993, Russia tried it.
The mirror was a thin sheet of foil, about 20 meters wide, unfolded near the Mir space station.
It aimed sunlight at Earth, making a bright spot about 5 kilometers across.
The spot looked about as bright as a full moon, and it swept across Europe in minutes.
A second try in 1999 failed when the foil snagged on an antenna and tore.
So a space mirror works, but it lights a patch for moments, and astronomers hated the idea.
